abstract: We give a deterministic online binary search tree (BST) that satisfies the unified bound of Iacono [SODA 2001], which subsumes the working-set and dynamic-finger bounds: it serves every sequence $X$ of $m$ searches on $n$ keys at total cost $O(m+\mathrm{UB}(X))$, and every single search at cost $O(\log n)$. Previously, no BST was known to satisfy the unified bound, even offline. As a consequence, the dynamic optimality conjecture implies Iacono's conjecture that splay trees satisfy the unified bound. We also show that the unified bound is $O((m+n)(1+\log c_\sigma))$ on every sequence of searches that avoids a fixed permutation $\sigma$, where $c_\sigma$ is the F\"uredi-Hajnal limit of $\sigma$. Hence every BST that satisfies the unified bound, including ours, serves such sequences at this cost. For permutations this bound is tight, and it improves the previous upper bound $O(nc_\sigma^2)$ on the optimal cost, due to Berendsohn, Kozma and Opler [STOC 2024]. Finally, we extend the tree to support insertions and deletions: a sequence $X$ of $m$ operations, starting from $n_0$ keys, costs $O(n_0+m+\mathrm{UB}(X))$ in total, where $\mathrm{UB}$ is now the extension of the unified bound to insertions and deletions by B\u{a}doiu, Cole, Demaine and Iacono [TCS 2007]. Hence, if splay trees are dynamically optimal for searches, insertions and deletions, then they serve every such sequence at this total cost as well.
hook: A binary search tree meets the unified bound, which no such tree was known to do before.
summary: The authors build a deterministic binary search tree whose cost on any search sequence matches Iacono's unified bound, which covers both the working-set and dynamic-finger bounds. They extend it to insertions and deletions and tighten the cost for sequences avoiding a fixed pattern. The result is a theoretical cost bound; it is not tested on real workloads.
title: A Binary Search Tree with the Unified Bound
